title: AusMT build report v1.0
description: Structured per-survey build metadata emitted alongside build_provenance.json: what each survey built, its structured survey-scoped warnings, the canonical-conditioning notes aggregated BY DISTINCT NOTE with station counts (the same aggregation the survey-level build log prints), the C18 cache counters, and per-survey wall time. Public build metadata for the (planned) curator serve-state UI.

engine_commit.description: short HEAD of the engine repo (mirrors build.json)

source_commit.description: short HEAD of the ausmt-surveys checkout, or null for --raw / non-git --surveys (mirrors build.json)

build_id.description: the opaque C12 build id (mirrors build.json)

pipeline_version.description: the engine distribution version (mirrors build_provenance.json's pipeline_version)

peak_rss_mib.description: the build process's memory high-water mark in MiB, read from resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss (KiB on Linux, bytes on macOS, normalised) at the moment this report is written: after the survey loop and the per-station products, before the corpus-wide manifest/mtcat/feed emissions (measured at ~10 MiB). Recorded so every real build carries its own peak and the trend is visible before a box runs out of memory (the 2026-08-15 OOM kills at 13.7 GB were the first sign). null where the counter is unavailable (Windows). Optional for pre-fix reports.

pages.description: the number of tier-3 landing pages written under pages/ (survey, station and collection pages plus the two hub pages). pages/ is outside the download manifest by design, so this is the build's only record that it wrote them, and the same count the sitemap reconciliation is run against. Absent on a build without --sitemap-base, which writes no pages at all, and on reports that predate the key.

surveys_skipped_validation.description: the LOUD skip (survey-metadata lane, D20): the package directory names the survey validator FAILed and the build SKIPPED (the build still exits 0 and the rest of the corpus builds). Empty on a clean build. scripts/verify.py FAILs on a non-empty list so `make rebuild-data` never swaps in a build that silently lost a survey from every public surface. Optional for reports that predate the gate; verify.py treats absence as unverifiable.

surveys_dropped.description: D20's rule extended to every OTHER survey-granularity drop (unreadable or non-mapping survey.yaml, invalid coordinate policy or station_ids block, a zero-station parse, an unserialisable SMETA): recorded here with its reason, empty on a clean build, and scripts/verify.py FAILs on any entry. Optional for reports that predate the gate.

stations_dropped.description: structured per-station drops: the C25 convention-gate FAILs (which name the gate, the angles and the fix), the stations whose coordinates or periods could not be recovered, and the source files mt_metadata could not read at all (whose reader error is also carried, typed, in source_parse_failures)

file.description: the name of the source file this station was dropped from. A drop row is the whole record for a station the corpus does not publish, and the only action it can lead to is opening that file; `station` is the id the build settled on, which for a third-party release is not the file's name (Roxby Downs 2018 withholds RD18-188e, whose source is 188_S__2.edi). Every drop path writes it. NOT required, because scripts/verify.py --data-dir validates a build_report already on disk, which during a rollback or a pre-swap check is one an older engine wrote without it.

tipper_masked.description: stations whose placeholder tipper (|T| flat at 1.0) was masked and withheld (C20 D2 honesty): the NOTICE's machine-readable twin, emitted identically on a C18 cache hit and a fresh parse. Optional for pre-fix reports.

xml_failures.description: per-station EMTF-XML emission failures: the station id and the exception class raised by normalize(). The CONSEQUENCE depends on the station's entry in ingest_sources, so this field does not state one: an EDI-sourced station falls back to serving its custodian EDI and loses only the XML download, while an emtfxml-sourced station has no custodian file behind it and serves NO bytes at all. Neither leaves an unverified rendition in the served tree. Empty when every served station's XML emitted; also surfaced as a counted `warnings` entry so a green build cannot hide the gap. Optional for pre-fix reports.

error.description: the exception class name raised by normalize() for this station

ingest_sources.description: the ingest source per BUILT station, keyed by station id: 'edi', 'mth5' or 'emtfxml'. Derived from the suffix of the input file the record was parsed from, so a mixed survey records which stations the EDI-wins precedence rule resolved to EDI and which came from EMTF XML. Optional for pre-EMTF-XML-ingest reports.

source_parse_failures.description: per-station record of source files mt_metadata could not read AT ALL, and that no normalised reparse rescued: the negative twin of source_parse_fallbacks. Each row is a DROPPED station and also carries a {station, reason} row in stations_dropped, which is where drop COUNTS are read; this array exists because stations_dropped has no room for the reader's own error, and a curator needs it beside the file name to tell a malformed header from a reader defect. Until the GDS readers lane these failures printed to stderr and continued, writing no record at all, so a station could vanish from a green build unremarked. The stations_dropped row raises the survey warning; this array raises none of its own, so one lost station is counted once. Empty for every survey whose files all read; optional for pre-fix reports.

station.description: the source file's stem, which is all the identity a file that never parsed has

error.description: the reader's own exception type and message

source_parse_fallbacks.description: per-station record of source files that mt_metadata could NOT read directly, and that were reparsed from a NORMALISED TEMPORARY COPY. The known case is mt_metadata 1.0.9's >INFO JSON trailing-delimiter defect: it strips JSON quoting from every line, mis-detects a JSON >INFO block as Empower format, and then keeps JSON's structural member separator in the scraped value, so a typed field receives a string such as '5,' and refuses it. This field is a PROVENANCE fact, not a repair log. The normalised copy is parse-only and is destroyed before the read returns: it is never served, never hashed for the integrity gate, and never copied into the output tree, so this station's served bytes and its catalogue sha256 are still the custodian's unmodified file. Also raised as a counted survey warning so a green build cannot hide it. Empty for every survey whose files are read directly; optional for pre-fix reports.

defect.description: what the reader could not do, and what was reparsed instead

source_section_selections.description: per-station record of which data section a MULTI-section source file's transfer function came from, and how many sections were left unread. An EPI-KIT file records its solution twice over: one >=MTSECT block carries the averaged solution named <DATAID>_avg, and after it come the per-frequency realisations XPR-0..XPR-n. mt_metadata rebinds each data block as it meets it, so an unconditioned read returns the LAST section, which is one sparse realisation rather than the transfer function of record. AusMT reads the section of record instead (<DATAID>_avg, else the section named for the DATAID, else the first), from a temporary copy carrying that section alone; the served bytes and the catalogue sha256 are still the custodian's unmodified file. A PROVENANCE fact, not a repair log, and also raised as a counted survey warning. WRITTEN ONLY WHEN IT FIRES: a survey whose files each carry one section (which is every survey in the corpus at the time this was added) carries no such key at all.

sectid.description: the SECTID of the section the transfer function was read from

sections_dropped.description: how many other data sections the file carries and this build did not read

source_integrity.description: the served-bytes integrity gate for EDI-sourced stations. AusMT serves a custodian's EDI byte for byte and never rewrites it, so each build re-hashes what actually landed in the served tree and compares it to the supplied file. `checked` counts the stations whose bytes were copied, `verified` those whose served copy hashed equal. A mismatch is a GATE, not a note: that station's served file is removed, it gets no manifest row and it serves no bytes at all, and it is also raised as a counted survey warning. Optional for pre-gate reports.

conditioning.description: one entry per DISTINCT canonical-conditioning note, ordered by first appearance

frame.description: C25 frame/convention notes (derotation records, convention WARNs, insufficient-data notes), same aggregation shape as conditioning; optional for pre-C25 reports

presence.description: the presence rule (station-schema freeze gate 15), same aggregation shape as conditioning: the mt_metadata library defaults each station's parse carried instead of a source assertion (run id '<station>a', a 0 Hz rate, the 1980 MTime epoch window, an unnamed data logger, a 0-ohm contact resistance, the rr* remote-reference channels). A REPORT of what the emitter refuses to publish as a source assertion, not a conditioning decision AusMT made, which is why it is a field of its own. Optional for reports that predate the rule

run_extraction.description: keyed by station id: which >INFO dialect produced that station's acquisition values and the extraction-confidence class behind each one (station-metadata scope section 6). station.json publishes the value alone, so this is where the class is kept, and it is the difference between a rate a structured dialect stated and one pattern-matched out of a processing token. Stations whose >INFO asserted nothing are omitted. Optional for reports that predate the extractors

digest.description: first 12 hex of the survey.yaml digest, or '' for --raw

conditioning_entry.description: a distinct conditioning note carried by `count` of the survey's note-carrying stations. At most one of `stations` (the small carrier set) / `except` (the small absentee complement) is non-null; both null => neither side is short enough to enumerate and the count alone tells the story.

dialects.description: the dialect extractors that recognised this station's >INFO

confidence.description: keyed by the value's path within the extraction (run.<key>, channels.<component>.<key>)
